record.paper_title: Geometric curvature energies: facts, trends, and open problems
record.context_brief: Regularity of critical points for curve energies
record.original_question: For geometric curvature energies on curves, can one prove additional regularity beyond the fractional Sobolev regularity that characterizes the energy spaces for local minimizers or critical points of the tangent-point energy, defined by integrating the inverse p-th power of the tangent-point radius between pairs of points on a curve, or of integral Menger curvature, defined by integrating the inverse p-th power of the circumradius over triples of points on a curve? If such extra regularity exists, does the optimal regularity depend on the exponent p, what happens to that p-dependent regularity as p tends to infinity, and does that limiting behavior give new information about the still-open optimal regularity of ideal knots?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\gamma:\mathbb{S}^1\to\mathbb{R}^3$ be a simple closed rectifiable curve, parametrized by arc length. For distinct points $x,y$ on the image of $\gamma$, let $r_{\mathrm{tp}}(x,y)$ denote the tangent-point radius, defined as the radius of the unique circle that is tangent to $\gamma$ at $x$ and passes through $y$; equivalently,
$$r_{\mathrm{tp}}(x,y)=\frac{|x-y|^2}{2\,\mathrm{dist}(y-x,\,\mathrm{span}\,\gamma'(x))}.$$
For distinct points $x,y,z$ on $\gamma$, let $R(x,y,z)$ denote the circumradius of the triangle with vertices $x,y,z$. For an exponent $p$, define the tangent-point energy
$$\mathcal{E}_p(\gamma):=\int_\gamma\!\!\int_\gamma \frac{1}{r_{\mathrm{tp}}(x,y)^p}\,d\mathcal{H}^1(x)\,d\mathcal{H}^1(y),\qquad p\geq 2,$$
and the integral Menger curvature energy
$$\mathcal{M}_p(\gamma):=\int_\gamma\!\!\int_\gamma\!\!\int_\gamma \frac{1}{R(x,y,z)^p}\,d\mathcal{H}^1(x)\,d\mathcal{H}^1(y)\,d\mathcal{H}^1(z),\qquad p\geq 3.$$
It is known that finiteness of $\mathcal{E}_p$ or $\mathcal{M}_p$ characterizes membership of $\gamma$ in certain fractional Sobolev–Slobodeckij spaces (the "energy spaces").

Address the following:

(a) Despite the degeneracies in the corresponding non-local Euler–Lagrange equations, prove or disprove that every local minimizer, or more generally every critical point, of $\mathcal{E}_p$ (respectively $\mathcal{M}_p$) admits additional regularity strictly beyond the fractional Sobolev regularity of its energy space.

(b) Determine whether the optimal regularity of such critical points depends on the exponent $p$, and if so describe this dependence explicitly.

(c) Analyze the behavior of the $p$-dependent optimal regularity in the limit $p\to\infty$.

(d) Use the limiting behavior from (c) to obtain new information about the optimal regularity of ideal knots (length-minimizers under a thickness constraint, equivalently minimizers of the limit energy as $p\to\infty$).
artifact.status_search_result: Partial results exist: smoothness of stationary points has been established in non-degenerate sub-critical regimes of (generalized) tangent-point energies TP^(p,q), e.g., for q=2 and p∈(4,5), and regularity of locally critical embeddings has been shown for scale-invariant tangent-point energies. However, the general question of optimal p-dependent regularity for critical points of E_p and integral Menger curvature M_p, the p→∞ limit, and consequences for ideal knot regularity remain open.

status_evidence.title: Regularity theory for tangent-point energies: The non-degenerate sub-critical case
status_evidence.snippet: Stationary points of TP^(p,2) + λ·length for p∈(4,5), λ>0, are smooth (non-degenerate sub-critical case).
status_evidence.claim: Higher regularity has been proven in a sub-critical non-degenerate regime of tangent-point energies, but not in full generality.

status_evidence.title: Scale-invariant tangent-point energies for knots
status_evidence.snippet: Regularity of locally critical embeddings is demonstrated for scale-invariant tangent-point energies; minimizing sequences converge to locally critical embeddings outside finitely many points.
status_evidence.claim: Partial regularity results exist for scale-invariant tangent-point energies, leaving optimal p-dependent regularity and ideal-knot limit open.
